design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (seller_standing_reviews_account_actions), revision 4 (policy-task audit revision_2 reworked)

[Routing decision, carried from round 2] The blueprint is frozen. Its standing product has no numeric field on a seller-owned act, and base fixes expiry and reversal amounts to a violation's recorded points. Reinstatement is excluded because standing_reinstate always triggers payout:payout_hold_release. Every computed value in this difficulty is therefore a whole number of violation points booked on a standing_events points-expiry entry. Every write lowers standing_records.violation_points by exactly its points, so the field stays the running sum of the ledger (base accounts.violation_points.meaning). Departures from base policy sentences are declared clause by clause in overwrite.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [4, 4]: clean-span relief 4 factors, action-plan relief 4 factors.

[Scope] Claimed here:
- standing_ext_clean_span_relief (agent, state_due, grant_clean_span_relief_513362ca);
- standing_ext_action_plan_relief (user, on_request, apply_action_plan_relief_841772f9).
Task 1 claims the listing expiry, the serious step-down, the top-performer relief and the closure. Scopes are disjoint and jointly complete.

[Audit revision_2 — responses by item id; round-1 closures kept]
- F-5 (suspension and appeal ladders treated a suspension overturned as Northloop's error as a blemish): closed by replacement.
  - Every factor that read reinstated_date or the appeal table is removed: clean-span suspension_history_credit; top-performer history and appeal-record credits; the closure's suspension_history_hold.
  - Replacements read seller-performance evidence only:
    - clean-span relief: repeat_record_credit (no type recorded more than once in twelve months 2 / one type twice 1 / otherwise 0);
    - top-performer relief: severity credit (no serious points 1 / serious points only from violations six or more months old 0.5 / a serious violation in the last six months 0) and remediation credit (FBN disposal in six months 1 / return 0.5 / none 0);
    - closure: at-risk hold (at_risk at or above the warning threshold 2 / at_risk below it 1 / good_standing 0).
  - No rule now reads suspension or appeal history, so no error-overturned suspension can lower a seller's relief or raise a hold.
  - Both worlds no longer seed a suspension episode. Here the record has never been suspended (reinstated_date empty, no appeal rows), and the persona answers 'never' if asked.
  - All scored values are unchanged: clean-span 5 (repeat credit 1 replaces the history credit 1), action-plan 3.
- F-T0-3 (stale ledger sums in proof fields): closed. With the episode removed, the seed records 18 points (4 + 2 + 8 + 2 + 2), none reversed, 6 expired: 18 - 0 - 6 = 12. The seed-consistency check, the clean-span factor trace and the clean-span points tracing now state these figures. Every other sum and date in this file was swept against the current seed.
- O-17 (persona sentence duplicated): closed. The suspension sentence is gone (no suspension on record) and replaced by a single line: asked whether the account was ever suspended, the seller says never.
- O-3 (narrowed only): no further change possible. The 'received' test reads any points-expiry entry dated three or more whole months after the latest violation. All removal entries share one row shape (O-4, schema frozen). Here the only entry after the latest violation is dated two months after it, so the clean-span write is the single write that brings the action-plan prerequisite state about.
- O-5 (narrowed only): answered in task 1's dossier, where the step-down applies. No serious violation in this world has run its first period (the intellectual_property violation of 2026-03-26 reaches six months on 2026-09-26).
- O-13 (appeal-credit gap for withdrawn or submitted appeals): closed. The appeal-record credit is removed.
- O-14 (closure tool contract changed under the same uuid8): closed. The tool was renamed with a fresh uuid8, close_selling_account_c808e333, in task_tools.py, the charter and task 1.
- O-15 (unstated four-decimal guard): closed. Every rule whose compute rounds through RND(..., 4) now states "products are worked to four decimal places before any rounding down".
- O-16 (retiring points on closure versus carry-forward): kept as designed and answered in task 1's dossier.
- Round-1 items remain closed as the audit confirmed: F-1, F-2, F-3, F-4, F-T0-1, F-T0-2, O-1, O-6, O-8, O-11. Still answered: O-2, O-4, O-7, O-9, O-10, O-12. The changes add no method factor and remove no honest one; every multi-source and cross-difficulty factor of this task is untouched.

[Why a good test] The seller asks only for her action-plan relief. Its rule says it "is fixed only after the standing record carries a points-expiry entry for every clean-span relief owed on it". The activity shows four whole months without a violation, and the only later entry is a routine expiry two months after the last violation. So clean-span relief is owed and not booked. The agent must book it first (5 points), then compute the seller's figure on 7 active points instead of 12 (3 instead of 4). The clean-span computation combines four inputs: a level-and-count rate, a band method that changes shape against the warning threshold, a repeat-record credit and a tenure cap. The action-plan computation combines a level-and-count share, a coverage method decided by FBN disposal evidence in another difficulty's records, a listing clean-span bonus and a tenure cap.

[Problem-tree card] Root action-plan relief (user) <- clean-span relief (agent).
- Edge: value_input, gate ap_active, state form, affirmative sentence "Action-plan relief is fixed only after the standing record carries a points-expiry entry for every clean-span relief owed on it."
- Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state; names no tool or id; scope 'every clean-span relief owed'.
- The only write of this difficulty that books a clean-span relief is the clean-span tool.
- False at the opening: latest violation 2026-05-06; the only later entry is dated 2026-07-14, fewer than three months after; 12 active points.
- Skipping the edge: action-plan relief 4 instead of 3 (terminal points 8 instead of 4).
- user_scenario names no prerequisite, and the tools check none.

[Base-invariant card] Both writes are points-expiry entries governed by standing_violation_rules.
- Gates expiry_due and reverse_once are replaced for these writes by declared overwrites.
- What stays in force: the entry goes against an active violation of the record (the intellectual_property violation, which has no removal before step 8).
- Scope: status good_standing/at_risk (at_risk); clean-span levels Below Standard to Above Standard (Above Standard).
- No other obligation falls due today:
  - listing expiry: period 8 (mid-level start 5, extension 2 for three violations counted with the serious one, disposal offset 1 for the 2026-07-29 disposal); the remaining listing violations (2026-04-22, 2026-05-06) are both four whole months old, so nothing has run;
  - step-down: the intellectual_property violation's first period runs on 2026-09-26 (five whole months now; 2026-09-25 is not owed, 2026-09-26 is);
  - top-performer relief: level not in scope;
  - no suspension: 12 < 16.

[Business-object card] One standing record. Active points 12: intellectual_property 8, listing_policy 2 + 2.
- The clean-span entry goes to the violation carrying the most points, the intellectual_property violation, leaving it 3.
- The action-plan entry goes to the same violation (3 against 2 and 2), and the 3 fits exactly.
- Both entries carry the type intellectual_property.

[Factor cards]
Clean-span relief (expected 5, all-baseline 2):
- rate (multi-source): Above Standard with 3 violations in twelve months -> 0.3; baseline 0.2 -> 4. Near-miss: the listing_policy violation of 2025-09-14 is exactly twelve months back; counting it gives 4 violations and the standard rate.
- band method: 12 >= 8 with clean span 4 -> graduated 8 x 0.3 + 4 x 0.6 = 4.8 -> 4; flat 12 x 0.3 = 3.6 -> 3 -> 4.
- repeat-record credit: listing_policy twice in twelve months -> 1; baseline 0 -> 4. Near-miss: the 2025-09-14 listing_policy violation would make three and drop the credit to 0 -> 4.
- tenure cap: 917 days -> 6, not binding; baseline 4 -> 4.
Action-plan relief (expected 3, all-baseline 1):
- share (multi-source): Above Standard with 2 listing-type violations in twelve months -> 0.35; baseline 0.25 -> 2. Near-miss: the 2025-09-14 violation at twelve months.
- coverage method (cross-difficulty fulfill): disposal fee 2026-07-29 -> all 7 points; baseline listing_policy points 4 -> 2. Near-miss: the return-to-seller fee of 2026-03-06 is outside three months.
- listing clean-span bonus: latest listing violation four months back -> 1; baseline 0 -> 2.
- tenure cap: 4, not binding; baseline 2 -> 2.

[Seed design] Seller only, never suspended; no orders or payments rows. Standing violations:
- restricted_product 4 on 2025-05-05, expired 2026-01-05 under the listing expiry rule as it stood (period 8: start 5, extension 1, offset 2);
- listing_policy 2 on 2025-09-14, expired 2026-07-14 under the rule then (period 10: start 6 because of a listing violation in the three months before, extension 2, offset 2);
- intellectual_property 8 on 2026-03-26: at_risk from that day, points 2 -> 10;
- listing_policy 2 on 2026-04-22 and listing_policy 2 on 2026-05-06 (peak 14 < 16).
FBN: Growth Program, 1,265 units; a return-to-seller removal (36 x 0.97 = 34.92, 2026-03-06) and a disposal (48 x 0.49 = 23.52, 2026-07-29), each with its removal order. Every seeded row is read by a gold lookup.

[Persona] Imogen opens with the request and her remediation, and gives email and tax last four when asked (phone spare). She answers the must-ask questions: first application, never suspended. Her reactions are passive, and she closes when told the application went through.

[Standard solution and recomputation] Reads: find_customers(business_name) -> verify(email, tax last4) -> find_seller_standing -> find_seller_standing_activity -> find_fbn_enrollments -> find_fbn_activity -> find_fbn_removal_orders. Writes:
1. clean-span relief (intellectual_property violation, 5) at step 8;
2. hand over the action-plan relief (intellectual_property violation, 3) at step 10.
Recomputed with the gate's evaluator on each handling-time world (scratch harness): clean-span 5 (factor baselines 4/4/4/4, all-baseline 2); action-plan 3 (2/2/2/2, all-baseline 1), 4 if the clean-span entry is skipped. A draft from the published rules, tool schemas, finder returns and persona alone reaches the same order, objects and figures.


[KB audit (policy_kb revision_1) — responses by note; no change to standing.extended.yaml or task_tools.py]
- Note 1 (point_expiry_days, 180 calendar days, survives in the base parameters): no change. The parameter belongs to the frozen base charter and must stay verbatim in the extended copy. The calendar-day clause that used it is retired by declared overwrites in every extended policy, and the KB states it is not applied. In this world no 180-day reading changes either figure.
- Note 2 (split of an aggregated expiry or step-down amount across several violations): no change. In this world no listing violation has run its period and no serious violation has run its first period, so neither amount arises. The relief bookings here pin their own order ('the active violation that still carries the most points, the oldest of them where two carry the same; the rest against the next'). Pinning the expiry and step-down split would need a charter change, which the coordinator asked to avoid after the KB audit, and no world in this difficulty reaches the case.
- Proof sweep: every figure, date and sum in this file was re-checked against the current seed and recomputed with the gate evaluator; no stale or false figure was found. The ledger reads 18 recorded - 6 expired = 12; then clean-span 5 and action-plan 3; the skipped-edge figure is 4 with terminal points 8; factor baselines are 4/4/4/4 and 2/2/2/2.
user_scenario:
You are Imogen Vasquez-Thorne, owner of Thornfield Pantry Goods, a small kitchen-and-pantry shop that sells on Northloop. You are practical, a little worn down by the orange 'at risk' banner on your account health page, and you talk in short, businesslike sentences. You open by giving your name and your business name, Thornfield Pantry Goods, and you explain that you have finished working through the account health action plan Northloop gave you for the listings that were flagged earlier this year: you fixed or took down every listing concerned, and back in late July you had the flagged stock pulled out of the fulfillment center and destroyed. You want to apply today for the action-plan relief on your violation points. You understand that the application is something you submit yourself; you want the agent to work out the exact figure and tell you exactly what to enter, and you will submit it while you are still on the call.
Only when the agent asks you to confirm who you are do you give your registered email, imogen.vasquezthorne@thornfieldpantry.com, and the last four digits of your tax ID, 9126; if they want one more detail you give your mobile number, 6175550537. You do not know the reference numbers of your violations or of your standing record and you tell the agent to look them up. You do not remember your exact points total; all you know is that the dashboard says 'at risk'. If the agent asks whether you have applied for this relief before, you say no, this is the first time. If the agent asks whether the account has ever been suspended, you say no, never.
If the agent tells you that something has to be booked on your record before your application can be worked out, you say that is fine and they can go ahead. When the agent reads you the details and hands the application over to you, you submit it with exactly the details they read out (the standing record reference, the violation reference, the violation type and the number of points) and then tell them what the confirmation showed. If the agent gives you a figure without saying how it was reached, you ask once how they got it, and you accept whatever they explain. Once the agent confirms that your application went through and your active points are lower, you thank them and end the call. You do not ask for anything else today.

factor_trace: clean_relief_rate (parameter, multi-source: level on the standing record AND a twelve-month count of violation records): Above Standard Level; violations recorded in the last twelve whole calendar months 2026-03-26, 2026-04-22, 2026-05-06 = 3 (the listing_policy violation of 2025-09-14 is twelve whole months back and excluded); tier 'Above Standard Level AND at most three' -> 0.3; baseline: standard rate 0.2 -> 8 x 0.2 + 4 x 0.4 = 3.2 -> 3 + 1 = 4.

clean_relief_band_method (method): active points 12 at or above the warning threshold 8; clean span MONTHS(2026-05-06, 2026-09-14) = 4, below six; tier 'at or above the threshold AND clean span below six months' -> threshold points at the rate and the 4 points above it at twice the rate: 8 x 0.3 + 4 x 0.6 = 4.8 -> 4; baseline (all active points at the rate): 12 x 0.3 = 3.6 -> 3 + 1 = 4.

repeat_record_credit (parameter): violation records in the last twelve whole calendar months by type: listing_policy 2 (2026-04-22, 2026-05-06), intellectual_property 1; the listing_policy violation of 2025-09-14 is twelve whole months back and does not count; tier 'a type recorded twice and none more often' -> 1; baseline: no credit -> 4.
clean_relief_tenure_cap (parameter): record opened 2024-03-11, 917 days; tier 'at least 730 but fewer than 1,095 days' -> cap 6, not binding; baseline: standard cap 4 -> 4.
plain bindings: active points = 18 recorded - 0 reversed - 6 expired = 12; result = MN(6, 4 + 1) = 5.
